ac:rich-text-body.p: Updated 28 Nov 2026. Use cases re-ordered. The earlier combined Editor and Reviewer look-up is now two use cases: Editor auto-assignment (POC 5) and Reviewer look-up and proposal (POC 6), which works on Reviewer availability, applicability for the selected journal, capacity and past experience with similar manuscripts. Every use case has a functional flow and architecture diagram and a technical process flow.

p: Six AI-based use cases are proposed for proof of concept. POC 1 to 3 build the manuscript profile, fit and readiness signals; POC 4 to 6 reuse them to route the manuscript and staff it with an Editor and Reviewers. Each runs on the Base AI Framework (section 9), reuses the TR microservices and AWS services in sections 7 and 8, and keeps the Editor in control of every decision. Success criteria are proposed targets, to be confirmed against a baseline from historical manuscripts.

td.p: Generate a structured, source-grounded summary of every manuscript (aims, methods, key findings, novelty claims, topics and entities) for the Editor Triage Workspace, and keep it current across revisions.
Summary & Fit agent (manuscript.summarize), sequential runtime

At least 85% of summaries rated accurate and useful by Editors on a sample; zero unsupported statements (every statement linked to a manuscript passage); P95 under 60 seconds; revisions regenerate only changed sections.

p.strong: POC 2: MSC fitment for a Journal

td.p: For the journal a manuscript was submitted to, assess how well it fits that journal's scope and editorial criteria, with related-research evidence, to support the Editor's early decision.
Summary & Fit agent (scope.assess), sequential runtime with retrieval

Fit assessment agrees with the Editor's early decision (proceed, transfer or decline) in at least 80% of a historical sample; every assessment cites evidence; Editor triage time reduced by at least 30%.

p.strong: POC 3: MSC validation and Integrity Check

td.p: Validate every new manuscript, and every revision, on arrival, then screen it against a common set of integrity parameters plus the parameters configured for the target journal, and present explained signals and a score to the Editor.
Integrity Check agent (integrity.screen) on the parallel runtime

At least 90% agreement with manual validation and integrity checks on a sample of past manuscripts; every finding linked to evidence; P95 under 5 minutes per manuscript; at least 50% fewer model calls on revisions through result reuse.

p.strong: POC 4: MSC Transfer to another journal

td.p: When the review or editorial assessment concludes that a manuscript fits another ACS journal better, recommend destinations within the Author's authorization and transfer it with the same manuscript identity and the history the receiving journal may see.
Transfer agent (destination.recommend), advanced runtime with human in the loop

Recommended destination accepted by the Editor in at least 70% of transfers; transfer completed with the same manuscript ID and no re-keying; no transfer outside the Author's authorization; transfer time cut by at least 50%.

p.strong: POC 5: Editor auto-assignment when an MSC appears on the Dashboard

td.p: As soon as a manuscript appears on the journal's dashboard, find the eligible and available Editors and assign the Handling Editor automatically when the journal's policy allows it and the recommendation is confident.
Editor Recommendation agent (editor.recommend), advanced runtime with human in the loop

Editor assigned within minutes of the manuscript reaching the dashboard; auto-assigned or top-ranked Editor accepted in at least 80% of cases; zero conflict-of-interest violations; time to assignment cut by at least 50%.

p.strong: POC 6: Reviewer look-up and proposal for MSCs without a Reviewer

td.p: For every manuscript on the dashboard that has no Reviewer assigned yet, look up and propose the best Reviewers based on Reviewer availability, applicability for the selected journal, capacity and past experience with similar manuscripts.
Reviewer Recommendation agent (reviewer.recommend), advanced runtime with human in the loop

At least 70% of invited Reviewers come from the top 5 proposed; zero proposals of unavailable, over-capacity or conflicted Reviewers; Reviewer acceptance rate above the current baseline; time from Editor assignment to first invitation cut by at least 50%.

h3: i. Functional flow and functional architecture

p.em: Figure 10. POC 1 functional flow and functional architecture

h3: ii. Technical solution architecture and design

td.p: ManuscriptParsed → Context & Enrichment (SQS subscriber) → Agent Connector opens a manuscript.summarize run on the sequential runtime.
Summary & Fit agent on AgentCore Runtime; Claude on Bedrock with versioned prompt templates per article type (Bedrock Prompt Management); Bedrock Guardrails contextual grounding check.
Long manuscripts are summarized section by section and then combined; Textract extracts figure and table text, and Comprehend extracts entities and key phrases.
Summaries and section fingerprints in DynamoDB with an ElastiCache read cache; source files in S3; topics and entities indexed in OpenSearch.
GET /triage/cases/{caseId}/summary; POST …/summary/feedback; publishes SummaryReady, which feeds ContextReady.

The summary, topics and entities are reused by POC 2 (fitment), POC 4 (transfer), POC 5 (Editor auto-assignment) and POC 6 (Reviewer look-up); prompt caching for shared instructions; only changed sections are regenerated.

p.em: Figure 11. POC 1 technical process flow (one row per architecture layer; numbered steps show the order)

h2: 10.b POC 2: MSC fitment for a Journal
h3: i. Functional flow and functional architecture

p.em: Figure 12. POC 2 functional flow and functional architecture

h3: ii. Technical solution architecture and design

td.p: Opening a case in the Editor Triage Workspace (or ContextReady) → Context & Enrichment requests a scope.assess run on the sequential runtime.
Summary & Fit agent on AgentCore Runtime; Claude on Bedrock for the assessment and explanation; Guardrails for grounding so every claim cites a source.
Knowledge Bases on OpenSearch with the journal's scope and criteria, its recent publications and a related-research index (Crossref metadata).
Journal criteria in Aurora PostgreSQL (Workflow & Policy Config); assessments in DynamoDB, cached in ElastiCache per manuscript version.
GET /triage/cases/{caseId}/scope-fit; PATCH /triage/cases/{caseId} for the disposition; publishes ScopeAssessed.

Criteria are per journal, not global, so journals keep their own standards; the manuscript profile from POC 1 (MSC summary) is reused to avoid repeat model calls; a poor fit can start POC 4 (transfer).

p.em: Figure 13. POC 2 technical process flow (one row per architecture layer; numbered steps show the order)

h2: 10.c POC 3: MSC validation and Integrity Check
h3: i. Functional flow and functional architecture

p.em: Figure 14. POC 3 functional flow and functional architecture

h3: ii. Technical solution architecture and design

td.p: ManuscriptParsed event → Integrity Orchestrator → Agent Connector opens an agent run with skill integrity.screen; the Step Functions Parallel state fans out one branch per parameter.
Submission and completeness rules (V-01 to V-16 in the MSC Validation and Integrity Rules catalogue) run in Submission & Parsing before screening; gaps go back to the Author.

Common and journal-specific integrity parameter sets (I-01 to I-22) stored as versioned configuration in Workflow & Policy Config (Aurora PostgreSQL); each parameter maps to a capability in the capability registry.
Integrity Check agent on AgentCore Runtime; Claude on Bedrock for policy and statement checks grounded in a Knowledge Base of journal guidelines; Bedrock Guardrails for PII and grounding.
MCP tools through AgentCore Gateway for iThenticate (similarity), Crossref (references), ORCID (identity), image forensics and COI / sanctions screening, each with a timeout and circuit breaker.
Files in S3; parsed text from Textract and Comprehend; findings and execution fingerprints in DynamoDB; hot results in ElastiCache.
POST /triage/cases/{caseId}/agent-runs; GET …/integrity-findings; PATCH /triage/integrity-findings/{id} for override; publishes IntegrityAssessed.
Parallel runtime with no orchestration reasoning for speed and cost; incremental processing reuses results for unchanged sections; partial results recorded if a vendor is unavailable.

h2: 10.d POC 4: MSC Transfer to another journal
h3: i. Functional flow and functional architecture

p.em: Figure 16. POC 4 functional flow and functional architecture

h3: ii. Technical solution architecture and design

td.p: DecisionRecorded (transfer suggested, from review or a poor fit in POC 2) → Transfer & Portfolio Routing requests a destination.recommend run; after selection a Step Functions saga runs consent, package build and handoff.
Transfer agent on AgentCore Runtime, reusing the manuscript summary and topics from POC 1; Claude on Bedrock for the rationale; Guardrails; human-in-the-loop checkpoints for selection and consent.
Authorization and routes in Aurora PostgreSQL; transfer package in S3 (versioned, KMS); history visibility rules per destination applied when the package is built.
Receiving journal notified through EventBridge API destinations; Author consent request and notices sent through SES; status synced back to Chronosub.
GET …/destination-recommendations; POST /triage/cases/{caseId}/transfers; POST …/transfers/{id}/rollback; publishes DestinationRecommended, ManuscriptTransferred.
Saga with compensating steps undoes a failed transfer; manuscript ID preserved; authorization checked before recommending and again before transfer.

h2: 10.e POC 5: Editor auto-assignment when an MSC appears on the Dashboard
h3: i. Functional flow and functional architecture

p.em: Figure 18. POC 5 functional flow and functional architecture

h3: ii. Technical solution architecture and design

td.p: A manuscript reaches the dashboard (Triage & Work Queue publishes MscQueued once ContextReady arrives) → Editor Assignment requests an editor.recommend run at once. Advanced runtime (graph) with a human-in-the-loop checkpoint.
Per journal in Workflow & Policy Config (Aurora PostgreSQL): auto-assignment on or off, confidence threshold, Editor board and maximum load per Editor.
Editor Recommendation agent on AgentCore Runtime; SageMaker ranking model trained on past assignments and overrides; Claude on Bedrock for the explanation text.
Expertise and conflict graph in Neptune; Editor profiles indexed in OpenSearch; live workload and availability in ElastiCache; assignments in Aurora PostgreSQL.

Assign automatically when the journal policy allows it, the top candidate passes eligibility and conflict checks, has capacity, is available and the score is above the threshold; otherwise route to the Assignment Console for the Assignment Authority.
GET /triage/cases/{caseId}/editor-recommendations; POST /triage/cases/{caseId}/assignments; publishes EditorRecommended, EditorAssigned; the dashboard updates over WebSocket.

Optimistic locking prevents double assignment; an Editor decline re-runs the ranking without that Editor; manual assignment is always available if the agent is unavailable; overrides feed model retraining.

h2: 10.f POC 6: Reviewer look-up and proposal for MSCs without a Reviewer
h3: i. Functional flow and functional architecture

p.em: Figure 20. POC 6 functional flow and functional architecture

h3: ii. Technical solution architecture and design

td.p: The dashboard lists manuscripts with no Reviewer assigned → ReviewerLookupRequested (on EditorAssigned, on dashboard load for unassigned manuscripts, and on a declined or expired invitation) → Reviewer Mgmt & Invitation requests a reviewer.recommend run. Advanced runtime with a human-in-the-loop checkpoint.

Four parameters (table below): availability, journal applicability and capacity act as gates and add to the score; past experience with similar manuscripts carries the largest weight. Conflict of interest is always a hard exclusion.

Reviewer Recommendation agent on AgentCore Runtime; embeddings of the POC 1 summary compared with the manuscripts each Reviewer has reviewed; SageMaker ranking model for the weighted score; Claude on Bedrock for a short reason per parameter.

Reviewer pool, journal eligibility, subject areas and availability calendar in Aurora PostgreSQL; live open-review counts in ElastiCache; review-history vectors in OpenSearch; conflict graph in Neptune.
A "Proposed Reviewers" panel per manuscript: the top 5 with a score and one reason per parameter; the Handling Editor picks and invites in one step.
GET /triage/cases/{caseId}/reviewer-candidates; POST /triage/cases/{caseId}/reviewer-invitations; publishes ReviewerCandidatesProposed, ReviewerInvited.
Step Functions handles invitations, reminders and expiry; a decline or expiry re-runs the look-up without that Reviewer; weights are configurable per journal; manual search is always available.

p: Reviewer selection parameters. A gate removes a Reviewer from the proposal; the weighted score ranks the Reviewers who pass every gate. Weights are proposed defaults, configurable per journal.
